metadata.scenario_context: Jake is graduating from his masters degree and his friends, Alex and Sam, plan to go to his graduation ceremony.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada strongly agree that whenever science and religion conflict, religion is always right.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Andorra strongly disagree that whenever science and religion conflict, religion is always right.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose on an expensive gift for Jake's graduation.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward the conflict between scientific treatment and religious beliefs.

agent_2.goal_1: discuss what kind of gift to buy for Jake.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is acceptable to forgo scientific treatment because of religious beliefs.

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: Hey Sam, have you thought about what gift we should get Jake for his graduation? I was thinking something really special... maybe a nice watch or an expensive piece of tech. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: Hmm... a watch could be nice, but I think we should consider something more personal. Maybe a custom item that reflects his journey. A tech gadget is cool, but it might not hold the same sentimental value. What about a personalized book or something related to his field?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but a custom item might not be as practical. I mean, a high-end watch is something he can use every day, a reminder of this achievement. It just seems more fitting for a milestone like this. Plus, it’s something he can keep forever. Wouldn't that be more special?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about practicality, but I still think a custom item can be both meaningful and useful. A watch is a nice idea, but it feels a bit generic to me. We want something that truly represents Jake and his hard work. Maybe we can find a balance? What if we combined the two ideas?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: Combining ideas could work, but I still lean toward something more universally appreciated... like a watch. It's a classic gift that everyone can relate to. A custom item might not resonate with him as much as something that symbolizes success and achievement. It’s about celebrating his hard work in a more tangible way. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: I understand that a watch is a classic choice, but I still believe we should focus on what makes Jake unique. Celebrating his success is important, but it should also reflect his personality and interests. It’s about making the gift special *for him*, not just a traditional milestone gift. Don't you think a more personalized approach could convey that better?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: I see your perspective, but I really think gifts should also be practical. A high-quality watch has both style and functionality. It can symbolize his journey while also being something he uses daily. It’s just... more versatile. I mean, sometimes the traditional route works best, right?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex
shared_prefix.message: At the end of the day, it’s all the same when it comes to gifts. A watch or a custom item, people figure it out based on what they value. I don't really see meaningful differences here, you know? I get that practical gifts have their charm, but we’re just celebrating Jake's achievement in our own way. Let's keep it simple. Did you have any ideas for the custom gift we could consider?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.message: Well, I still think a watch stands out more in this context. But if we're going the custom route, maybe we could look into a personalized book? Something that reflects his journey or achievements, like a collection of quotes from his field. Still, I feel like it wouldn’t hit the mark like a nice watch would. But I’m open to your suggestions if you really want to pursue this.
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Alex
turns.message: A personalized book could be a great choice, especially if it highlights his achievements and includes meaningful quotes. It can be a source of inspiration for him. I appreciate you being open to different ideas. But I still think we shouldn’t overlook the significance of a gift that’s uniquely tailored to him. It doesn’t have to be one or the other. Maybe we can come up with a unique way to present the book, like a nice custom cover or something?
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: It sounds like both of you have really thoughtful ideas about what makes a gift special, but I wonder if there might be some cultural influences at play here. Sam, you seem to value practicality and tradition, while Alex, you’re leaning towards personalization and uniqueness. How do you both feel about the role that culture plays in gift-giving? Could exploring that help you find common ground?
